# `•r` — Regular expressions

`text •r pattern` gives a table of the matches of the regular expression `pattern` in `text`, as a record of columns: `text`, the matched text; `position`, its position in characters from 0; and `groups`, the text of each group, which is empty for a group that took no part. [`•replace`](replace.qmd) replaces matches. BPL keeps the 16 patterns it compiled last, so a loop that uses one pattern compiles it once.

Natively the pattern uses [fancy-regex's syntax](https://docs.rs/fancy-regex/latest/fancy_regex/#syntax), including lookaround and backreferences. Flags go in the pattern, as in `(?i)`. A search that exceeds the engine's backtracking limit raises `DOMAIN`. In the browser the pattern is a JavaScript regular expression, with [JavaScript's syntax](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Regular_expressions). [Regular expressions](../regex.ipynb) covers matching and replacing.

```bpl
"ab12 cd3" •r "([a-z]+)([0-9]+)"   ⍝ ["text":["ab12" "cd3"] "position":[0 5]ₓ "groups":("ab" "12"◇"cd" "3")]
```

Errors: `DOMAIN` for invalid patterns and non-text arguments; `SYNTAX` for the wrong valence; `LIMIT` for oversized results.
